payload.statement: UniProtKB natural variant VAR_002690 at residue 226 (R to C): X-linked severe combined immunodeficiency; Combined immunodeficiency, X-linked; XSCID. 1 publications cited.
Ensembl VEP predicts missense_variant for NM_000206.3:c.676C>T (NP_000197.1:p.Arg226Cys; exon 5/8; MANE Select ENST00000374202.7).
UniProtKB annotates residues 219-226 of P31785 as Beta strand; evidence: combinatorial computational and experimental evidence used in automatic assertion.
The study reports that Arg226Cys (R226C) is located in the extracellular domain, a region the authors describe as important for receptor stability.
UniProtKB annotates residues 156-253 of P31785 as Domain: Fibronectin type-III; evidence: match to sequence model evidence used in manual assertion.
Molecular dynamics simulations of a homology model showed that the variant exhibited structural instability, whereas wild-type IL2RG remained stable.
InterPro annotates residues 154-253 of P31785 as domain: Fibronectin type III; evidence: match to sequence model evidence used in automatic assertion.
The study reports that R226C reduced hydrogen bonds to decrease binding in protein-protein docking with IL-2, and that both variants displayed weaker interactions with IL-21.
AlphaMissense gives p.Arg226Cys of P31785 a AlphaMissense pathogenicity of 0.5785, classed as likely pathogenic (AlphaMissense class) (scale: 0 to 1; higher = more likely pathogenic).
payload.strength: computational prediction, not validated for clinical use

payload.statement: 14 of 14 experimental structures of P31785 in the Protein Data Bank observe residue 226.

No retrieved experimental study measures R226C protein expression, surface trafficking, or cytokine-binding affinity; the only mechanistic source is an in-silico homology model with MD and docking.
payload.why_it_matters: Without wet-lab data it is unclear whether R226C acts mainly through folding and stability loss, through impaired surface expression, or through a direct defect at the cytokine interface.

payload.statement: The retrieved literature does not report whether R226C impairs downstream JAK3/STAT5 signalling in cells.
payload.why_it_matters: Signalling readouts would show whether the predicted weaker cytokine binding translates into lost receptor function at the cell level.

payload.statement: The Arg226Cys substitution sits in a beta strand (residues 219-226) of the fibronectin type-III domain of IL2RG. Losing the charged, buried-side-chain Arg and adding a smaller Cys destabilises that strand and the domain fold, so less correctly folded receptor reaches the surface.
payload.would_refute: Computed stability change for R226C versus wild type (for example FoldX or Rosetta ΔΔG on the AlphaFold DB model or a PDB template) is near zero or stabilising, and molecular dynamics of R226C versus wild type over matched replicates show no difference in backbone RMSD or strand H-bond persistence around residue 226.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Ranked first because E7 is the only retrieved structural observation of this exact variant (MD instability of the R226C model versus stable wild type), and it sits in a conserved beta strand of the FN-III domain (E4, E6, E12) with high pathogenicity scores (E10, E15). Still weak: E7 comes from one homology model with no experimental stability or expression data (G1), and no structure with residue 226 mutated exists (G5), so the stability reading has not been tested independently.

payload.statement: Residue 226 lies at or near the IL-2 / IL-21 / IL-4R-binding surface of IL2RG. Arg226Cys removes the Arg side chain's hydrogen bonds and charge contacts with the cytokine, so the receptor binds IL-2 and IL-21 more weakly and signalling through the common gamma chain is lost.
payload.would_refute: Cytokine-bound experimental structures (9E2T, 5M5E) place residue 226 with no atom within about 4.5 Å of IL-2, IL-21 or IL-4R partner chains, and docking or free-energy calculations of R226C versus wild type show no change in interface contacts or binding energy beyond the spread between replicate runs.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Ranked second because the interface evidence is also about this exact variant (E9 fewer hydrogen bonds and weaker IL-21 binding; E11 MM/PBSA gap) and two cytokine-bound structures observe residue 226 (E17, E18). It is weaker than the stability hypothesis because E9 and E11 rest on the same single homology model and docking run (G3), the cytokine-complex contact map is not reported (G6), and no binding affinity was measured (G1).

payload.summary: Two agent-generated hypotheses are recorded: H1 stability_folding (rank 1) and H2 protein_interaction (rank 2). Both are testable computationally. Priority tests: ΔΔG and MD replicates for H1, and contact distances from 9E2T/5M5E plus R226C docking for H2. The record has no experimental binding, expression or signalling data (G1, G2, G4, G5).

payload.description: FoldX predicted folding free-energy change (ddG) of R226C on the AlphaFold model via EBI ProtVar, with pLDDT at residue 226 and the predictor's values for other disease substitutions at this residue. A destabilising ddG supports H1 (stability_folding); a neutral or stabilising value weakens H1 and leaves H2 (protein_interaction) as the main explanation.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: This is the only available test that separates the two hypotheses on opposite predictions. H1 predicts a destabilising ddG; H2 predicts a neutral one, because H2 is about binding and not fold. A destabilising value would strengthen H1 and move H2 down. A neutral value would move H1 down and H2 up. The ranking is therefore expected to change, but the result is a prediction with about 1 kcal/mol error, and a neutral value does not rule out H1, so the learning is capped at moderate.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: list_available_tests reports can_run true and FoldX state 'ok' for this substitution. It needs no compute seconds and no approval, and it takes 2 tool calls. The value is not shown before the run, so the score is not 1.
controls: Within-site comparison: the same predictor for the other substitutions reported at this residue.
Applicability control: the model confidence (pLDDT) at the residue, because FoldX on a low-confidence region is not interpretable.

payload.description: Whether R226 lines a pocket predicted by P2Rank or ProtVar on the AlphaFold model, and whether it lies in a ProtVar-predicted protein-protein interface. Membership of a predicted interface supports H2 (protein_interaction). No interface membership weakens H2 and leaves H1 (stability_folding) as favourite.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: This test checks H2's location claim, which is the premise of H2. If R226 is in a predicted interface, H2 gains and the ranking may flip. If it is not, H2 is weakened. The result is less decisive than the stability test, because predicted interfaces are coarse and a pocket hit says little about cytokine binding. Also, the current ProtVar interface state is None, which suggests a negative outcome already. A negative result would mostly confirm what the record already implies, so the expected change is limited.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: list_available_tests reports can_run true. ProtVar pocket and interface data answer for this residue, and P2Rank runs on the AlphaFold model. It needs no compute seconds and no approval, and it takes 2 tool calls.
controls: Rank control: the rank and probability of the pocket among all predicted pockets of the model.
Confidence control: mean pLDDT of the pocket residues.

payload.description: Checks whether R226 is a neighbour of a non-solvent ligand in the 12 experimental structures that cover the residue and hold a ligand. This bears on ligand binding, not on H1 (folding) or H2 (cytokine interface), so it does not test either hypothesis directly.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: The catalogue lists ligand_binding as the only hypothesis class this test bears on, and neither H1 nor H2 is that class. A ligand contact with a soluble analogue, or none at all, would not separate stability_folding from protein_interaction. The test's own limitation, that a crystal contact is not a measurement of binding by the variant protein, makes any outcome weak. Expected change in ranking is close to zero.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: list_available_tests reports can_run true with 12 experimental structures that observe residue 226 and hold a non-solvent ligand. It needs no compute seconds and no approval, and it takes 2 tool calls.
controls: Negative control: ligands in the same structures that never list the residue as a neighbour.
Selectivity control: number of distinct residues that neighbour the contacting ligand, so a contact is not an artefact of a large neighbour list.
Site-state control: structures in which the residue itself is mutated are reported separately.

payload.description: Predicts the reference and R226C construct (residues 1-369) with the same provider and compares local and global C-alpha RMSD, site pLDDT and contact changes. A confident local rearrangement supports H1; a matching fold is uninformative about H2.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A local rearrangement would support H1. A matching fold, which is the most likely outcome for a single substitution, tells us nothing about H2 and little about H1. Structure predictors are not validated for single-residue substitutions, and each model runs once, so run-to-run noise is not estimated. The expected change in ranking is modest.

payload.rationale: The objective asks for one targeted computational test to pick the mechanism, so I compared the four candidates on expected learning, feasibility and cost. T1 (stability_effect) has learning 0.6, feasibility 0.9 and cost 0 compute seconds, 2 tool calls, no approval. It is the only candidate whose outcome points in opposite directions for H1 and H2: a destabilising ddG supports H1, and a neutral value favours H2. T2 (structural_context) scores 0.35 at the same cost, so it is weaker. T3 (ligand_contact) scores 0.1 because it bears on ligand binding, which neither hypothesis claims. T4 (structure_comparison) scores 0.3 with feasibility 0.1: it needs approval, 120 compute seconds, and the ESM provider is not answering. The budget has 300 compute seconds and 107 tool calls left, so T1 fits easily. Scores are my own; no earlier result changed the choice, since this is the first round.

rejected.reason: structural_context: learning 0.35 at zero cost. It checks the location premise of H2, but the predicted interface state is already None, so a negative result would mostly confirm the record. Its outcome is also coarse. Keep as a follow-up if T1 is neutral.

ligand_contact: learning 0.1. It bears on ligand binding, which is neither H1 nor H2, and the test's own limitation (a crystal contact with a soluble analogue is not measured binding by the variant) makes any outcome uninformative for the ranking.

structure_comparison: learning 0.3 and feasibility 0.1. It needs human approval and 120 compute seconds, and the ESM Atlas provider did not answer within 20 s with no cached output. It cannot run now, and a matching fold would be uninformative for H2.

per_hypothesis.why: T1 FoldX ddG for R226C is +0.51 kcal/mol on AF-P31785-F1 (residue pLDDT 96.69), below the 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold. H1 predicted a destabilised strand. The refutation criterion needs both a near-zero or stabilising ddG and an MD null result. The ddG half is met, the MD half is not tested, so H1 is weakened, not refuted. Literature MD instability (E7) and pathogenicity predictors (E10, E14, E15) are unchanged, but they do not replace the missing stability signal.

T1 measures folding stability, not cytokine binding. It does not bear on whether R226 contacts IL-2, IL-21 or IL-4R, so the H2 evidence (E9, E11, E17, E18, E20) is unchanged. H2 remains untested on its own refutation criterion.

payload.uncertainty: FoldX on a single predicted model has errors near 1 kcal/mol, so +0.51 is not clean proof of no destabilisation. Controls: R226H +10.76 and R226L +0.59 show the predictor does separate substitutions at this site, but R226L is close to R226C, so the scale is coarse. Stability in a model does not show tolerance in vivo. The MD refutation arm for H1 and any interface test for H2 are still not done. The T1 result also does not carry the in-silico literature MD result (E7), which used a homology model, not the AlphaFold model. Validation still needed: a second stability predictor, the MD matched-replicate run, and contact measurements in the experimental cytokine complexes (9E2T, 5M5E).

payload.why: Previous favourite H1 (stability/folding) was weakened by T1: FoldX ddG +0.51 kcal/mol for R226C (below 2.0 threshold; pLDDT 96.69), per E4, E6, E10, E12, E14, E15. Its refutation criterion was only half met (no MD arm), so it is not refuted. Strongest rival H2 (interface) was not addressed by T1, so it gains nothing from it, but it no longer trails H1 on the direct stability premise. H2's direct support is E9 and E11 (IL-2/IL-21 binding weaker, MM/PBSA), E17/E18 (residue 226 observed in cytokine-bound structures), and E20 (IL4R interaction). That support is still indirect, because the contact test has not been run. Favour H2 with low confidence. Test IDs: T1. Evidence IDs: E9, E11, E17, E18, E20, E4, E7.

payload.description: Computational contact and interface test on the experimental cytokine complexes 5M5E (IL-2 / IL2RG) and 9E2T (IL-21 / IL-21R / IL2RG). Measure the minimum heavy-atom distance from R226 side-chain atoms to the IL-2, IL-21 and IL-4R partner chains. Then run FoldX AnalyseComplex on each complex for R226C versus wild type and report the interface ddG. Outcome that supports H2: R226 within 4.5 A of a partner chain, and an interface ddG for R226C above the replicate spread. Outcome that refutes H2: no atom of R226 within 4.5 A of any partner, and interface ddG within the replicate spread. This is the H2 would_refute criterion.
payload.why_now: T1 weakened the stability route for H1 and left H2 untested, so the next step must test the H2 interface premise directly. The T2 ProtVar interface check returned no interface data, so a direct contact measure on the experimental complexes is needed. It is cheap and uses data already in the record (E17, E18, E20).

per_hypothesis.why: T2 does not measure stability. R226 falls in ProtVar pocket 3 (buriedness 0.77, mean pLDDT 97.3), which fits the buried-residue premise of H1, but that location is not diagnostic of a folding defect. The folding test (T1, FoldX +0.51 kcal/mol, below the 2.0 threshold) already weakened H1 and T2 does not change that.

H2 assumes R226 sits at or near the cytokine-binding surface. T2 reports no predicted protein-protein interface (in_predicted_interface null, ProtVar: residue in no predicted interface) and places R226 in a buried pocket (buriedness 0.77). The P2Rank pocket test found no pocket containing R226 (1 pocket total). This weakens the location premise. It is not refuted: the refutation criterion needs contact distances to IL-2/IL-21/IL-4R in 5M5E and 9E2T and docking or free-energy results, and none of those were run here.

payload.uncertainty: T2 uses predicted pockets and interfaces, not measured binding sites, and the AlphaFold DB model is a single monomer without cytokine partners, so it cannot show whether R226 contacts IL-2, IL-21 or IL-4R. The interface field is null, which means ProtVar returned no interface state, not a confirmed absence; treat it as no evidence of an interface rather than proof against one. Controls: the pocket is rank 3 of predicted pockets with mean pLDDT 97.3, so the location call is well-ordered; the P2Rank model reports one pocket that does not include R226. Still needed: contact distances from R226 to partner chains in the experimental complexes 5M5E and 9E2T, and a FoldX AnalyseComplex or docking comparison of R226C versus wild type. The E9 and E11 binding results are literature abstracts from a computational study with no citations and have not been reproduced here.

## Question
Which molecular mechanism best explains the loss of function of IL2RG p.Arg226Cys (UniProt P31785), and does one targeted computational test change the starting conclusion? ClinVar lists the variant as pathogenic for X-linked severe combined immunodeficiency [E1], and UniProt records it as an XSCID variant [E2].

## Evidence
Residue 226 lies in a predicted beta strand (219-226) of a fibronectin type-III domain [E4, E6]. A literature study reports MD instability of a homology model and weaker docking and MM/PBSA binding to IL-2 and IL-21 for R226C [E7, E9, E11]. That study is in-silico only and reports no experimental validation [E13]. No retrieved study measures expression, trafficking, or cytokine affinity [G1], or JAK3/STAT5 signalling [G2]. Residue 226 is observed in cytokine-bound structures 5M5E and 9E2T [E17, E18], and IntAct records an IL4R interaction without residue mapping [E20, G6].

## Agent-generated hypotheses
H1 (stability_folding, starting rank 1) and H2 (protein_interaction, starting rank 2) are agent-generated hypotheses [H1, H2].

## Tests considered and the choice
Round 1 chose T1 (stability_effect) over T2, T3 and T4 [T1]. Round 2 chose T2 (structural_context) after the reopening [T2]. T3 was rejected as bearing on neither hypothesis, and T4 was rejected for needing approval and an unavailable provider [T3, T4].

## Result
Prediction: FoldX ddG for R226C is +0.51 kcal/mol, below the 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold, with controls R226H +10.76 and R226L +0.59 [T1, E21, E22, E23]. Prediction: residue 226 lies in a buried predicted pocket and in no predicted protein-protein interface, and no P2Rank pocket contains it [T2, E24, E25].

## Updated decision
Before T1, H1 was favoured. After T1, H2 was favoured and the decision changed [H1, H2]. After T2, H2 stays favoured at low confidence, and both hypotheses are weakened [H1, H2]. H1 lost its stability premise, and H2 lost its location premise.

## Uncertainty and validation still needed
All results are computational predictions and are not validated experimentally. The T1 analysis calls the single-model FoldX query coarse [T1]. The T2 interface field is null, which the analysis treats as no evidence of an interface rather than proof of absence [T2]. The MD refutation arm for H1 and any contact or docking test for H2 were not run [H1, H2].

## Next experiment
Proposed next test, not yet run: measure minimum heavy-atom distances from R226 to partner chains in 5M5E and 9E2T, and run FoldX AnalyseComplex on R226C versus wild type, which is the refutation criterion for H2 [H2, E17, E18].
